selected.hook_line: How can one tiny atomic event decide a whole cat's fate?
selected.viewer_expectation: A change inside one atom seems too small to control something as large as a cat.
selected.visible_contradiction: A teaching rig connects one possible atomic decay to a chain that reaches the whole sealed cat setup.
selected.frame_zero: A transparent teaching rig shows a tiny radioactive source, detector, relay and large sealed cat-box model connected in one chain.
selected.character_action: He traces the chain from the tiny source to the detector, then to the much larger box.
selected.reaction: His eyes move back to the tiny source, doubtful that such a small event can start so much.
selected.activity: Following how a microscopic event can trigger a large physical consequence.
selected.location: A simple physics exhibit room with one clear cutaway mechanism.
selected.topic_link: A microscopic quantum event can be linked to a detector and mechanism that produces a large everyday outcome.
selected.factual_anchor: Schrödinger's thought experiment links a possible atomic decay to a detector and mechanism. One decay can trigger the chain, so microscopic alternatives become linked to different large outcomes.
selected.payoff: Show how the thought experiment carries uncertainty from one atom into two different cat-scale outcomes.

entry_bridge.a_end: He finishes tracing the mechanism and looks down beside the large box.
entry_bridge.b_start: Cut: the red host, fully visible, stands one step from the almost-closed red door laid as a floor hatch with safe steps below.
entry_bridge.reveal: The hatch clicks open onto a detector chain below; he steps down and crosses as the camera gently follows.
entry_bridge.world_entry: A host-free view follows one atomic event into a detector, relay and two diverging large-scale consequences.

novelty.reveal_family: the scale jump follows one physical chain
